summary: Field Shift is a decision-support tool that turns NASA Earth data into crop-rotation strategies farmers can simulate, compare and explain. It combines NASA POWER daily climate, official yields and margins from Argentina's agriculture ministry (MAGyP), local soil and crop information, and the farmer's own priorities. For any field it compares at least three rotations, including the current one, and stress-tests each over 22 real three-season climate windows (2001-2025), including the 2022/23 drought, checking extreme heat, frost, dry spells, water deficit and heavy rain day by day. A Farm-Wide Optimizer, a resilience profile (Field Shift DNA), a 3D Climate Twin and a rule-based Copilot help explore options. Every result states why it scores as it does, what evidence supports it and what must be validated by a local agronomist. It supports farmers; it never replaces their judgment.
details: What it does: for a field and a sowing date, Field Shift filters the crops that can grow there, scores the rest on six weighted priorities set by the farmer (income, speed, soil health, input savings, resilience, compliance) and explains each result. It compares at least three rotations, including the current one, and replays each over 22 real windows of three consecutive seasons (2001-2025) using daily NASA POWER data: extreme heat, frost, dry spells, water deficit (crop demand = Kc x ET0) and heavy rain. A Farm-Wide Optimizer searches combinations for the whole farm, a resilience profile (Field Shift DNA) explains what changes, a 3D Climate Twin replays a real campaign such as the 2022/23 drought, and a local rule-based Copilot answers questions and runs what-if scenarios such as irrigation. Data and evidence: NASA POWER (daily and monthly climate, MERRA-2 root-zone soil wetness, CERES-based solar radiation) at its regional resolution (about 55 x 60 km), not field-level measurements. Argentine official yields, prices and margins from MAGyP. A statistical yield-response model (ridge or random forest) was trained on 35 departments over 1981-2024 and validated leave-one-year-out against a trend-only baseline; a crop uses it only if it passes a criterion fixed beforehand. It reproduces past campaigns out of sample, it is not a forecast, and it softens extreme years. Intended impact: help farmers see, before planting, how rotations behave under dry and extreme seasons, and why, so they can decide with evidence. It supports farmers and never replaces farmer or agronomist judgment. Limits we state openly: the crop catalog, soils and rotation effects are illustrative and need local validation; NASA POWER is regional; there is no future-climate scenario because NASA POWER climate projections returned no data for Argentina. Tools: JavaScript (single-file static web app, PWA), Leaflet and Esri World Imagery for maps, three.js for the 3D twin, Python (pandas, scikit-learn) for the yield model, Vercel for hosting. Source code, documentation and a project wiki: https://github.com/BlasFerreira/nasa-hacka
